papers.title_en: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
papers.authors: Robin Hollifeldt, Tianru Zhang, Jessica Ström, Ekta Vats
papers.evidence: 面向重写本的注意力手写文本识别网络
papers.tldr: 针对重写本中被覆盖原文难以恢复且耗时的问题，本文探索GAN与扩散模型，并设计学习结构化噪声的自定义去噪扩散模型来重建底层文本。恢复结果再交由微调的注意力手写文本识别网络处理，并引入以文本类别描述为先验、经CLIP视觉注意力图落地的语言引导识别框架。该方法有助于从噪声中区分有意义特征，同时发布合成重写本数据集、CLIP兼容描述、预训练模型与代码，支撑后续研究与基准测试。
papers.abstract_en: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

papers.title_en: A Systematic Comparison of Search Space Complexity and Efficiency for Time-Synchronous End-to-End ASR Models
papers.authors: Simon Berger, Larissa Kleppel, Ralf Schlüter
papers.evidence: 对CTC搜索空间复杂度的比较分析
papers.tldr: 当前端到端ASR研究常把搜索简化为固定小束宽、无外部语言模型的束搜索，缺少对搜索空间复杂度的系统分析。本文对CTC与神经Transducer在不同剪枝策略和LM配置下的搜索空间复杂度与效率进行对比。结果显示模型多数时候只需很小搜索空间，但在不确定时段假设数会短暂激增；基于分数的剪枝能随模型不确定性自适应调整，显著降低实时率RTF。工作揭示了固定小束宽剪枝的局限，并为高效搜索提供实践指南。
papers.abstract_en: Search is a central component of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems and has been deeply investigated for classical ASR modeling based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). However, in work on current sequence-to-sequence ASR architectures it is often simplified to a small fixed-size beam search without external Language Model (LM). In this work, we present a comparative analysis of search space complexity and efficiency for Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and neural transducer models under different pruning strategies and LM configurations. We show that these end-to-end (E2E) models work with a small search space most of the time but exhibit large temporary peaks in hypothesis count during periods of uncertainty. Score-based pruning dynamically adapts the search to model uncertainty, leading to a significantly lower Real-Time Factor (RTF). Our results highlight the limitations of search with low fixed-size beam pruning and provide practical guidelines for efficient search in E2E ASR.
